description: Make PPT-derived Markdown searchable at slide/heading granularity by reusing the existing fenced-code-aware heading parser, bounding oversized sections at 8 KiB, and persisting the existing deterministic structure nodes in the disposable wiki index.

userStories.title: Chunk headed Markdown at section boundaries
userStories.description: As a retrieval user with PPT-derived Markdown, I need every slide heading to become a searchable chunk even when the whole file is small.
acceptanceCriteria: The shared chunker applies fenced-code-aware Markdown heading spans regardless of total page size; total file size no longer gates heading parsing.
The default maximum chunk size is 8 KiB for generated wiki and raw retrieval commands, and only an individual oversized section falls back to paragraph/UTF-8-safe splitting.
A small PPT-style Markdown fixture with one ATX heading per slide yields one heading-path chunk per slide plus only any legitimate preamble/root chunk.

A headingless document at or below 8 KiB remains one chunk, headings inside fenced code remain opaque, and every emitted chunk stays within 8 KiB unless one UTF-8 character would make that impossible.
Focused chunking, raw retrieval, and wiki index tests pass.
userStories.notes: Keep this story to chunk behavior, defaults, help text directly controlled by those defaults, and focused tests. Do not add wiki structure persistence yet.

userStories.title: Persist wiki heading structure and connect search hits
userStories.description: As a wiki retrieval user, I need each searchable section chunk linked to the existing deterministic heading tree so results identify their exact section without a new routing engine.
acceptanceCriteria: The disposable wiki index schema is bumped from wiki-heading-index-v8 to wiki-heading-index-v9 and adds a structure_nodes table plus chunks.node_id with deterministic foreign-key ownership; incompatible v8 indexes rebuild rather than migrate.
Rebuild stores the document root and every ATX heading node for every indexed wiki page by reusing structure_nodes_for_page, including pages below 8 KiB.
Each chunk has exactly one owning structure node; ordinary section chunks link to their matching heading node and legitimate preamble/headingless chunks link to the document root.
Existing lexical and semantic search result shapes remain compatible and add node_id; body hits retain heading_path and current line/byte routing ranges.
Exact title/path results may remain page-level, while body matches for headed content return the matching section path.
Doctor/schema validation detects missing tables, invalid parents, invalid chunk ownership, range violations, and row divergence without introducing tree/ancestor/subtree CLI commands.
Focused index, lexical, semantic, and raw retrieval tests pass.
checks: python3 -m unittest tests.test_wiki_sqlite_index tests.test_wiki_sqlite_retrieval tests.test_wiki_sqlite_semantic tests.test_wiki_raw_retrieval -v
userStories.notes: Reuse the raw index's proven ownership pattern. Do not add adaptive thresholds, migrations, ranking changes, a new database, or new public navigation commands.

userStories.title: Synchronize generated guidance and certify the patch
userStories.description: As a generated-vault maintainer, I need the documented retrieval contract and tests to match the new slide/section behavior and schema v9.
acceptanceCriteria: Generated AGENTS/README guidance describes heading-first chunks and 8 KiB as a per-section maximum rather than a whole-file activation threshold.
Current docs and wiki/_meta/log.md describe wiki v9 structure persistence, node-linked search results, and the unchanged Markdown-canonical boundary.
No adaptive chunk policy, PPT-specific parser, new workflow ledger, ontology layer, or new runtime dependency is introduced.
Repo Docs validation passes with zero errors and zero warnings for the branch changed-file set.
git diff --check passes and the final diff contains only intended product, tests, docs, and Ralph state changes.
userStories.notes: Update affected current docs and generated-text assertions in the same story. Keep SQLite explicitly disposable and Markdown canonical.
